title: The Imposter Phenomenon
shortDefinition: The persistent psychological pattern of doubting one's accomplishments and having an internalized fear of being exposed as a fraud.
dailyExample: Getting promoted or receiving glowing academic feedback and thinking: 'I just got lucky, they made a mistake, soon everyone will realize I know nothing.'
psychologyTheory: Identified by clinical psychologists Pauline Clance and Suzanne Imes (1978). It is especially prevalent among high achievers, marginalized groups, and people in competitive transitions.
inTherapy: We deconstruct external attribution ('It was just luck') versus internal agency ('I prepared and possess competence'), building grounded self-worth.
practicalTakeaway: Feeling like an imposter doesn't mean you lack ability; ironically, it usually means you care deeply about your craft and are pushing beyond your comfort zone.
